results.question: Under what two conditions must the Extended APN-AMBR information element be included in a message according to clause 8.3.18.14?
results.reference: It must be included only if both of the following are true: 1) at least one APN-AMBR value has been changed by the network, and 2) at least one of the values to be transmitted exceeds the maximum value specified in the APN aggregate maximum bit rate IE in clause 9.9.4.2.
results.model_answer:
According to clause 8.3.18.14 of 3GPP TS 24.301, the **Extended APN-AMBR information element** must be included in a message under the following two conditions:

1. **The network wishes to transmit the APN-AMBR values to the UE for possible uplink policy enforcement**, **and**
2. **At least one of the APN-AMBR values to be transmitted exceeds the maximum value specified in the standard "APN aggregate maximum bit rate" information element (defined in clause 9.9.4.2).**

These conditions are derived directly from the normative text provided in the context:

> *"This IE shall be included in the message only if the network wishes to transmit the APN-AMBR values to the UE for possible uplink policy enforcement and at least one of the values to be transmitted exceeds the maximum value specified in the APN aggregate maximum bit rate information element in clause 9.9.4.2."*

Thus, both conditions must be satisfied simultaneously for the inclusion of the Extended APN-AMBR IE.

results.question: Why would the Extended APN-AMBR information element be omitted from a message even if the network has modified an APN-AMBR value?
results.reference: It would be omitted if, despite the network changing an APN-AMBR value, none of the values to be transmitted exceed the maximum limit specified in the APN aggregate maximum bit rate information element (clause 9.9.4.2). Both conditions in the clause are required for inclusion.
results.model_answer:
The **Extended APN-AMBR** information element (IE) may be omitted from a message even if the network has modified an APN-AMBR value due to **specific inclusion conditions defined in the 3GPP TS 24.301 specification**.

Based on the provided context and standard behavior:

> *"This IE shall be included in the message only if at least one of the APN-AMBR values has been changed by the network **and** at least one of the values to be transmitted exceeds the maximum value specified in the APN aggregate maximum bit rate information element in clause 9.9.4.2."*

Additionally, another sentence reinforces this:
> *"This IE shall be included in the message only if the network wishes to transmit the APN-AMBR values to the UE for possible uplink policy enforcement **and** at least one of the values to be transmitted exceeds the maximum value specified in the APN aggregate maximum bit rate information element in clause 9.9.4.2."*

### Analysis:

- The **Extended APN-AMBR IE** is not unconditionally sent when APN-AMBR is changed.
- It is only included **if two conditions are both met**:
  1. The network has changed at least one APN-AMBR value.
  2. At least one of the new APN-AMBR values **exceeds the maximum value** that can be encoded in the standard **APN-AMBR IE** (defined in clause 9.9.4.2).

The standard **APN-AMBR IE** uses a 4-octet format with a maximum representable bit rate of **4,194,300 kbps (≈4.1 Gbps)**. If the updated APN-AMBR is within this range, the Extended APN-AMBR IE is **not needed**, because the value can be conveyed using the regular APN-AMBR IE.

However, if the new APN-AMBR exceeds this upper limit (e.g., >4.1 Gbps), then the **Extended APN-AMBR IE** must be used to carry the higher precision value.

---

### Therefore, the reason for omission is:

> ✅ **Even though the network modified the APN-AMBR, the new value(s) do not exceed the maximum bit rate supported by the standard APN-AMBR IE. Hence, the Extended APN-AMBR IE is not required and is omitted.**

This is consistent with the design principle of minimizing signaling overhead — use extended IEs only when necessary to convey values beyond the capacity of standard IEs.

---

### Conclusion:

🔹 The **Extended APN-AMBR IE is omitted** because **the modified APN-AMBR value(s) are within the range expressible by the standard APN-AMBR IE**, and thus there is no need to include the extended form, even if a change occurred.

The presence of the Extended APN-AMBR IE is **conditional on exceeding encoding limits**, not merely on a change in value.

results.question: What role does the maximum value from the APN aggregate maximum bit rate IE (clause 9.9.4.2) play in the inclusion of the Extended APN-AMBR IE?
results.reference: It serves as a threshold: the Extended APN-AMBR IE is included only if at least one APN-AMBR value to be transmitted is greater than this maximum value, provided that the network has also changed at least one APN-AMBR value.
results.model_answer:
The **maximum value from the APN aggregate maximum bit rate IE (defined in clause 9.9.4.2 of 3GPP TS 24.301)** acts as a **threshold** that determines whether the **Extended APN-AMBR IE** must be included in a NAS message.

Specifically, based on the provided context:

> *"This IE shall be included in the message only if at least one of the APN-AMBR values has been changed by the network and at least one of the values to be transmitted exceeds the maximum value specified in the APN aggregate maximum bit rate information element in clause 9.9.4.2."*

And alternatively:

> *"This IE shall be included in the message only if the network wishes to transmit the APN-AMBR values to the UE for possible uplink policy enforcement and at least one of the values to be transmitted exceeds the maximum value specified in the APN aggregate maximum bit rate information element in clause 9.9.4.2."*

### Role of the Maximum Value:
- The **APN-AMBR IE (standard)** can only carry APN-AMBR values up to a certain maximum limit defined by the encoding rules in **clause 9.9.4.2**, which specifies the format and range for the APN-AMBR.
- If the actual APN-AMBR value (either downlink or uplink) that the network intends to assign **exceeds this maximum representable value in the standard IE**, then the **Extended APN-AMBR IE is required** to convey the larger value.
- Therefore, the **maximum value in the standard APN-AMBR IE serves as a boundary**: only when the desired APN-AMBR exceeds this boundary is the Extended APN-AMBR IE included.

### Conclusion:
The **maximum value from the APN aggregate maximum bit rate IE (clause 9.9.4.2)** functions as a **conditional trigger** for including the **Extended APN-AMBR IE**:
- If any APN-AMBR value to be sent **exceeds** this maximum, the Extended APN-AMBR IE **must be included**.
- Otherwise, it is **not included**, assuming no other conditions require it.

Thus, its role is **to define the upper bound beyond which extended encoding is necessary**, ensuring backward compatibility and correct interpretation of high bit-rate values in evolved networks.

results.question: Under what conditions would the network send the Extended emergency number list IE, and what does its content signify?
results.reference: The network may send the IE. If sent, its content indicates a list of emergency numbers (with URN information) that are either valid within the same country as the PLMN from which the IE is received, or valid only in that specific PLMN.
results.model_answer:
The network sends the **Extended emergency number list IE** under the following conditions:

- The network may include the Extended emergency number list IE in the **ATTACH ACCEPT** or **TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT** messages.
- This inclusion is optional and at the discretion of the network, typically to provide the UE with additional local emergency numbers beyond those stored on the USIM or ME.

---

### **Significance of the Content:**

The **Extended emergency number list IE** contains one or more **local emergency numbers**, each associated with:
1. A **sub-services field** (zero or more sub-services) related to an emergency service URN.
2. An **associated emergency service URN**, which is a service URN with a top-level service type of `"sos"` as defined in IETF RFC 5031.
   - Example: `urn:service:sos.gas` indicates a gas emergency service.
   - If the URN is `urn:service:sos`, the sub-services field is empty (length = 0).
   - The URN can be standardized or country-specific as defined in 3GPP TS 24.229.

Each emergency number is encoded with its digits (using GSM 7-bit default alphabet for sub-services), and the structure includes validity scope information via the **Extended Emergency Number List Validity (EENLV)** field.

---

### **Validity Scope (from EENLV field):**

The validity of the list depends on the value of the **EENLV field** within the IE:
- If set to **"Extended Local Emergency Numbers List is valid in the country of the PLMN from which this IE is received"**:  
  → The list is valid for all networks in the same country as the sending PLMN.
- If set to **"Extended Local Emergency Numbers List is valid only in the PLMN from which this IE is received"**:  
  → The list is valid only within that specific PLMN.

> ⚠️ **Note:** To prevent misrouting, operators in a country should coordinate whether to set validity per-country or per-PLMN.

---

### **UE Storage and Update Rules:**

- The UE stores only **one instance** of the Extended Local Emergency Numbers List.
- The list is **replaced entirely** whenever a new Extended emergency number list IE is received.
- The list is **retained** across TAU/Attach procedures **only if**:
  - No new list is sent **and** the registered PLMN has not changed.
- The list is **deleted** when:
  - The PLMN changes **and** the last EENLV indication was "valid only in the PLMN", **or**
  - The UE switches off or removes the USIM.
- The UE can store up to **20 entries** in this list.

---

### **Usage by the UE:**

- The UE uses this list (alongside the Local Emergency Numbers List, USIM, and ME-stored numbers) to detect if a dialed number is an emergency number.
- However, **this list is not used when selecting the CS domain** for emergency calls — only the Local Emergency Numbers List applies in CS fallback scenarios.
- Matching stops upon first match (per NOTE 1).

---

### Summary:

| Aspect | Details |
|-------|--------|
| **When sent** | In ATTACH ACCEPT or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT (optional) |
| **Content** | One or more emergency numbers + associated URNs + sub-services |
| **URN Type** | `"sos"`-based URNs (e.g., `urn:service:sos.fire`) |
| **Validity** | Determined by EENLV field: per-PLMN or per-country |
| **Storage** | Replaces previous list; deleted on PLMN change (under certain EENLV conditions), power-off, or USIM removal |
| **Max Entries** | 20 |
| **CS Domain Use?** | ❌ Not used when CS fallback is selected |

This mechanism enables dynamic provisioning of regionally relevant emergency services, supporting regulatory and operational flexibility while ensuring correct emergency call handling.

results.question: What are the two possible scopes of validity for the emergency numbers listed in the Extended emergency number list IE when it is sent by the network?
results.reference: The numbers are either valid within the same country as the PLMN from which the IE is received, or they are valid only in the specific PLMN from which the IE is received.
results.model_answer:
The two possible scopes of validity for the emergency numbers listed in the Extended emergency number list IE are:

1. **Valid only in the PLMN from which the IE is received** – This applies when the Extended Emergency Number List Validity (EENLV) field indicates "Extended Local Emergency Numbers List is valid only in the PLMN from which this IE is received".

2. **Valid in the entire country of the PLMN from which the IE is received** – This applies when the EENLV field indicates "Extended Local Emergency Numbers List is valid in the country of the PLMN from which this IE is received".

These validity scopes are explicitly defined in the specification and determine how broadly the UE can apply the received emergency numbers, based on operator policy and national agreements.

results.question: How does the Extended emergency number list IE relate the validity of its emergency numbers to the PLMN from which it is received?
results.reference: The validity of the listed emergency numbers is defined relative to the originating PLMN: they are either country-wide (same country as that PLMN) or restricted solely to that specific PLMN.
results.model_answer:
The **Extended emergency number list IE** includes an **Extended Emergency Number List Validity (EENLV) field**, which explicitly defines the validity scope of the emergency numbers contained in the list relative to the PLMN from which it is received. The relationship between the list and the PLMN is determined by the value of this EENLV field:

1.  If the **EENLV field indicates "Extended Local Emergency Numbers List is valid in the country of the PLMN from which this IE is received"**, then the emergency numbers are valid for use in any network within the same country as that PLMN.

2.  If the **EENLV field indicates "Extended Local Emergency Numbers List is valid only in the PLMN from which this IE is received"**, then the emergency numbers are valid *only* within that specific PLMN and do not extend to other PLMNs, even if they are in the same country.

This mechanism allows the network to precisely control the geographical and administrative scope of the extended emergency numbers, ensuring they are used appropriately based on national regulations or operator agreements.

results.question: What information, besides the emergency numbers themselves, is included in the Extended emergency number list IE, and what determines the geographical scope of these numbers?
results.reference: The IE includes emergency numbers with URN information. The geographical scope is determined by the originating PLMN, specifying if the numbers are valid in the same country as that PLMN or only within that PLMN itself.
results.model_answer:
The **Extended emergency number list IE** includes the following information besides the emergency numbers themselves:

1.  **Emergency Service URN (Uniform Resource Name):**
    *   Each emergency number in the list is associated with a service URN.
    *   The URN has a top-level service type of "sos" as defined in IETF RFC 5031.
    *   Examples include `urn:service:sos` for general emergency or `urn:service:sos.gas` for a specific service like gas emergencies.

2.  **Sub-services Field:**
    *   This field contains zero or more sub-services related to the associated emergency service URN.
    *   For example, if the URN is `urn:service:sos`, the sub-services field might be empty. If the URN is `urn:service:sos.gas`, the sub-services field would contain "gas".
    *   The characters in this field are coded using the GSM 7-bit default alphabet.

---

The geographical scope of the numbers in the Extended Local Emergency Numbers List is determined by the **Extended Emergency Number List Validity (EENLV) field** within the same IE. This field indicates one of two scopes:

1.  **Valid only in the PLMN from which the IE was received:** The numbers are valid exclusively within the specific Public Land Mobile Network that sent them.
2.  **Valid in the country of the PLMN from which the IE was received:** The numbers are valid across all networks within the same country as the PLMN that sent them.

This validity information ensures the UE knows where it can appropriately use these extended emergency numbers.

results.question: How does the coordination between ESM and 5GSM procedures ensure proper handling of session management requests?
results.reference: The coordination is defined by referencing the equivalent procedures and rules specified in the 5GSM protocol, ensuring consistent behavior and conflict resolution when both ESM and 5GSM contexts are active.
results.model_answer:
There is **no direct coordination between ESM (4G) and 5GSM (5G) procedures defined within 3GPP TS 24.301**, as this specification governs only EPS (Evolved Packet System) session management for E-UTRAN (LTE), not 5GS (5G System). Therefore, **TS 24.301 does not define mechanisms for coordination between ESM and 5GSM procedures**.

However, based on broader 3GPP architecture principles (outside the scope of the provided context but aligned with inter-system mobility specifications such as TS 23.502 and TS 24.501), proper handling of session management across 4G and 5G is ensured through:

1. **Inter-system Mobility Procedures**: When a UE moves between E-UTRAN and NR (New Radio), session continuity is maintained via inter-system handover or redirection procedures (e.g., S1-based handover to NG-RAN or N26 interface-based handover). During these transitions:
   - The **MME** in 4G and **AMF** in 5G coordinate via the N26 interface (if available) to transfer EMM and ESM contexts to the AMF and SMF, respectively.
   - This allows ongoing EPS bearer contexts (managed by ESM) to be mapped into appropriate PDU Sessions (managed by 5GSM), preserving IP connectivity.

2. **Dual-Stack Operation and Interworking Modes**: UEs capable of both 4G and 5G operate in various interworking modes (e.g., EPS fallback, SA/NSA dual connectivity). In such cases:
   - Session management requests are routed according to the current access type.
   - If the UE is in connected mode via one system, session modification or new requests are handled natively in that system unless triggered by mobility.

3. **Separate Protocol Stacks with Context Transfer**: 
   - ESM operates over NAS between UE and MME in E-UTRAN.
   - 5GSM operates over NAS between UE and SMF (via AMF) in 5GS.
   - These are distinct protocol entities; coordination occurs at the architectural level during state transitions, not within the ESM protocol itself.

4. **No Concurrent Execution in Same NAS Instance**: A UE cannot simultaneously perform ESM and 5GSM procedures over the same NAS connection because:
   - Only one NAS protocol (EMM/ESM or 5GMM/5GSM) is active at a time depending on the registered network.
   - Transitions between systems involve registration updates and potential context forwarding.

### Conclusion:
Within **TS 24.301**, there is **no mechanism defined for direct coordination between ESM and 5GSM**, since it is specific to EPS. Proper handling of session management across 4G and 5G relies on higher-level architectural procedures defined in other specifications (e.g., TS 23.501, TS 23.502, TS 24.501), including inter-system handover, N26 interface context transfer, and UE state management — none of which are described in the provided excerpts.

Thus, **coordination is external to ESM and achieved through network-wide mobility and session continuity mechanisms, not via intra-specification interaction between ESM and 5GSM in TS 24.301.**

results.question: What is the purpose of having a dedicated clause for ESM and 5GSM coordination in this specification?
results.reference: To formally establish that coordination mechanisms exist between the two session management protocols and to direct implementers to the authoritative source for the detailed procedural requirements.
results.model_answer:
There is no dedicated clause for ESM and 5GSM coordination in **3GPP TS 24.301**, because **TS 24.301 specifically covers EPS (Evolved Packet System) Session Management (ESM) only**, which applies to **E-UTRAN (4G LTE)** access within the context of **EPS**.

The coordination between **4G ESM** and **5G 5GSM (5G Session Management)** is not handled in TS 24.301, but rather in other specifications that deal with interworking between EPC and 5GCN, such as:

- **3GPP TS 23.502**: *Procedures for the 5G System (5GS)* — This specification defines inter-system mobility procedures between E-UTRAN and NG-RAN, including how session management contexts are mapped and coordinated during interworking (e.g., N26 interface-based handover or registration).
- **3GPP TS 24.501**: *Non-Access-Stratum (NAS) protocol for 5G System (5GS)* — This is the 5G equivalent of TS 24.301 and contains 5GSM procedures.
- **3GPP TS 23.401**: *General Packet Radio Service (GPRS) enhancements for evolved UTRAN access* — Provides architectural aspects of EPS, including interaction with non-3GPP systems and interworking.

### Therefore:
**The purpose of not having a dedicated clause for ESM and 5GSM coordination in TS 24.301 is by design** — TS 24.301 focuses exclusively on **4G NAS signaling**, particularly EMM and ESM procedures in an **EPS-only or S1-mode context**. It does not extend into 5GS session management logic.

Coordination between ESM (4G) and 5GSM (5G) is instead addressed through:

1. **Inter-system mobility procedures** (e.g., from 5GS to EPS or vice versa), where mapping rules between EPS bearer contexts and PDU sessions are defined.
2. Use of the **N26 interface** between MME and AMF to transfer subscriber context, including PDN connections / PDU session states, during inter-system change.
3. Indications in messages like **Attach Request**, **Tracking Area Update**, or **Handover Required** that signal support for dual connectivity or interworking with 5GC.

In summary:  
👉 **TS 24.301 does not include a dedicated clause for ESM/5GSM coordination because it is outside its scope.**  
Such coordination is instead specified in system architecture (TS 23.502), interworking procedures, and the 5G NAS specification (TS 24.501), ensuring clean separation between 4G and 5G control plane protocols while enabling interoperability via standardized mappings and interfaces.

results.question: Why would a UE enter the EMM-REGISTERED.UPDATE-NEEDED substate?
results.reference: The UE enters this substate when it needs to perform a tracking area update but cannot access the current cell because access is barred, either due to access class control or network rejection of NAS signalling connection establishment.
results.model_answer:
There is **no such substate** as **EMM-REGISTERED.UPDATE-NEEDED** defined in 3GPP TS 24.301.

### Analysis:

The EMM (EPS Mobility Management) states and substates are strictly defined in 3GPP TS 24.301, particularly in **clause 5.2** ("EMM states and modes") and related procedures.

The valid **EMM-REGISTERED** substates include:
- **NORMAL-SERVICE**
- **ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE**
- **ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE-MM**
- **LIMITED-SERVICE**
- **PLMN-SEARCH**
- **NO-CELL-AVAILABLE**

Additionally, during specific conditions such as eCall-only mode with expired timers, the UE may transition to **EMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE**, but this is a deregistered state.

---

### Relevant Context from Specification:

From your provided context:
> "The substate EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE is chosen by the UE if the tracking area updating or combined tracking area updating procedure failed due to a missing response from the network or due to the circumstances described in clauses 5.3.9, 5.5.3.2.5, 5.5.3.2.6, 5.5.3.3.5, 5.6.1.5 and 5.6.1.6."

This confirms that when an update is needed after a failure, the correct substate is **EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE**, not "UPDATE-NEEDED".

Similarly, **EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE-MM** is used when CS fallback-related tracking area updating fails (e.g., cause #16 or #18), per the handling of EMM cause values.

---

### Conclusion:

➡️ The substate **EMM-REGISTERED.UPDATE-NEEDED** **does not exist** in 3GPP TS 24.301.

If a UE needs to perform a tracking area update (TAU), it will be in one of the following defined substates:
- **EMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE** — where periodic or event-triggered TAU is initiated normally.
- **EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE** — after a prior TAU failure.
- **EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE-MM** — when MM (non-EPS) registration also needs to be addressed.

Thus, the question assumes a non-existent substate.

✅ **Answer:**  
A UE would **not** enter an **EMM-REGISTERED.UPDATE-NEEDED** substate because **this substate does not exist** in 3GPP TS 24.301. The specification defines other substates (such as ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE) to handle cases where a tracking area update is required.

The substate that most closely matches the intent behind "UPDATE-NEEDED" is likely **EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE**.

In this substate, the UE has determined that a tracking area update (TAU) is required but has not yet initiated it — for example, due to temporary inability to establish a connection or because it is waiting for conditions to allow transmission.

### Procedures Allowed in EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE:

- If the UE initiates a Service Request or Extended Service Request while in `ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE`, it **must include a TAU request** in those messages (via the "active" flag or piggybacking).
- The UE remains in `ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE` until the TAU is successfully completed, unless interrupted by higher-priority events like detach or loss of coverage.

---

### Conclusion:

There is no such substate as **EMM-REGISTERED.UPDATE-NEEDED**.

If you meant **EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE**, then the UE is allowed to initiate:
- Tracking Area Updating Procedure
- Service Request Procedure (with piggybacked TAU)

Based on your question and the provided context, it appears you may be referring to a substate where the UE needs to perform a tracking area update (TAU), such as **EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE**, which *is* defined in the specification.

Let’s clarify the correct behavior based on the actual specification and the provided excerpts:

---

### Correct Substate: **EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE**

As stated in the context:

> "The substate EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE is chosen by the UE if the tracking area updating or combined tracking area updating procedure failed due to a missing response from the network or due to the circumstances described in clauses 5.3.9, 5.5.3.2.5, 5.5.3.2.6, 5.5.3.3.5, 5.6.1.5 and 5.6.1.6."

#### Restrictions on UE Behavior:
- **Only the tracking area updating or combined tracking area updating procedure shall be initiated** by the UE in this substate.
- **No other EMM procedure shall be initiated.**
- **No user data shall be sent or received.**

This means:
- The UE is in a restricted operational mode.
- It must re-attempt the TAU procedure (e.g., after a timer expires or upon cell change).
- It must not initiate any other EMM procedures such as detach, attach, or GUTI reallocation.
- NAS signaling for non-TAU purposes is prohibited.

Additionally, the UE remains in this substate until the TAU procedure is successfully completed or further recovery actions (like moving to EMM-DEREGISTERED) are triggered per failure handling rules.

---

### Conclusion:

There is **no valid substate called EMM-REGISTERED.UPDATE-NEEDED** in TS 24.301. The intended substate is likely **EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE**, in which case:

> ✅ The UE is **restricted to initiating only the tracking area updating or combined tracking area updating procedure**.  
> ❌ It **shall not initiate any other EMM procedure**, and **no data transmission (signaling or user data) is allowed**.

This ensures focused recovery of mobility registration without introducing conflicting state transitions.

results.question: Under what conditions does the MME use the default APN as the requested APN?
results.reference: When no requested APN is included in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST or ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE message, and the request type is not 'emergency', 'handover of emergency bearer services', or 'RLOS'.
results.model_answer:
The MME uses the default APN as the requested APN under the following conditions:

- The PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message does **not include a requested APN**, **and**
- The **request type is different from**:
  - "emergency",
  - "handover of emergency bearer services", and
  - "RLOS".

In such cases, according to the specification, the MME shall use the default APN for PDN GW selection.

### Rationale:
This behavior ensures that when a UE does not explicitly request an APN (e.g., during initial attach or when relying on subscription-based configuration), and the request is for normal connectivity (not emergency, RLOS, or emergency handover), the network applies operator-defined policies by selecting the default APN associated with the subscriber's profile. This aligns with standard EPS session management procedures where the default APN serves as the fallback for Internet or operator-specific services unless otherwise specified.

> ⚠️ Note: For emergency, emergency handover, or RLOS request types, the MME instead uses pre-configured APNs specific to those services, overriding any default APN logic.

results.question: Why must a UE not automatically send another PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST for a different PDN type after receiving ESM cause #50?
results.reference: The UE is prohibited from automatically re-requesting a different PDN type to the same APN until it registers to a new PLMN, is switched off, or the USIM is removed, as the network only allows IPv4 for that APN.
results.model_answer:
A UE must not automatically send another PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST for a different PDN type after receiving ESM cause #50 ("PDN type IPv4 only allowed") because the network has explicitly indicated that, for the requested APN, only IPv4 connectivity is permitted — either due to subscription limitations or network configuration.

According to 3GPP TS 24.301, when the UE requests a PDN type such as IPv4v6 but the network overrides this and returns ESM cause #50 (or #51), it means the network restricts the PDN type to IPv4 only. In such cases:

- The UE **shall not subsequently initiate another UE-requested PDN connectivity procedure** to the same APN to obtain a different PDN type (e.g., IPv6 or IPv4v6) **until one of the following occurs**:
  - The UE registers in a new PLMN,
  - The UE is switched off, or
  - The USIM is removed.

This restriction prevents the UE from repeatedly attempting incompatible PDN types that are administratively prohibited by the network for that APN. The rationale is to avoid unnecessary signaling and failed connection attempts when the network policy clearly defines a single allowed PDN type.

Furthermore, the specification emphasizes that any subsequent request for a different PDN type **must originate from upper layers**, not be automatically triggered by the UE’s ESM layer. This ensures explicit user or application-level intent before retrying under potentially changed conditions (e.g., in a different PLMN where policies might differ).

Thus, the prohibition on automatic retries with a different PDN type enforces compliance with network-imposed restrictions while allowing flexibility for future attempts when context changes.

results.question: Under what conditions must a network include the Negotiated LLC SAPI IE when supporting mobility from S1 mode to A/Gb mode?
results.reference: The network must include the Negotiated LLC SAPI IE only if the UE supports A/Gb mode.
results.model_answer:
A network supporting mobility from S1 mode to A/Gb mode must include the **Negotiated LLC SAPI IE** if the **UE supports A/Gb mode** and **the negotiated LLC SAPI is modified**.

### Reasoning:

From the provided context:

> "If the UE supports A/Gb mode and when the negotiated LLC SAPI is modified, a network supporting mobility from S1 mode to A/Gb mode shall include this IE"

This sentence directly specifies the condition under which the Negotiated LLC SAPI IE must be included by the network:

1. **UE supports A/Gb mode** – This is a prerequisite.
2. **The negotiated LLC SAPI is modified** – This triggers the requirement to include the IE.

Thus, both conditions are necessary:
- The UE must have A/Gb mode capability.
- There must be a modification of the negotiated LLC SAPI value.

If either condition is not met, the network is not required (by this rule) to include the IE.

Additionally, note that the Negotiated LLC SAPI is one of the **GERAN/UTRAN parameters** used during inter-system change to A/Gb mode (as listed in the NOTE on SM parameter usage). However, the specific inclusion requirement for this IE in signaling (e.g., in ESM messages like Bearer Context Modification) is governed by the conditional statement above.

### Conclusion:

✅ The network **must include the Negotiated LLC SAPI IE**  
→ **if and only if**:  
- The **UE supports A/Gb mode**, **and**  
- The **negotiated LLC SAPI is modified**.

results.question: How does UE capability influence the inclusion of the Negotiated LLC SAPI IE in mobility from S1 mode to A/Gb mode?
results.reference: The inclusion of the IE is conditional upon the UE's support for A/Gb mode.
results.model_answer:
The inclusion of the **Negotiated LLC SAPI IE** during mobility from **S1 mode to A/Gb mode** is directly influenced by the **UE's capabilities**, specifically whether the UE supports **A/Gb mode** and, optionally, **BSS packet flow procedures**.

### Key Conditions from 3GPP TS 24.301 (Implied by Context):

Although the provided context does not explicitly define the "this IE" referenced in the sentences, based on the repeated conditional structure:

> "If the UE supports A/Gb mode, a network supporting mobility from S1 mode to A/Gb mode shall include this IE"

and

> "If the UE supports A/Gb mode and BSS packet flow procedures, a network supporting mobility from S1 mode to A/Gb mode shall include this IE"

—and given that the question asks about the **Negotiated LLC SAPI IE**—we infer that “this IE” refers to information elements required for proper inter-system handover to GERAN (A/Gb mode), including **LLC SAPI** parameters.

In particular:
- The **LLC SAPI (Logical Link Control - Service Access Point Identifier)** is a parameter used in **GERAN A/Gb mode** to identify data flows at the LLC layer.
- During inter-system change from **S1 mode (E-UTRAN)** to **A/Gb mode (GERAN)**, the MME must provide certain UTRAN/GERAN-specific parameters to ensure continuity of PDP contexts corresponding to EPS bearers.
- One such parameter is the **negotiated LLC SAPI**, which is necessary for mapping EPS bearers to PDP contexts over A/Gb.

---

### Influence of UE Capability:

#### 1. **Support of A/Gb Mode**
- If the **UE does not support A/Gb mode**, there is no need for the network to prepare for mobility to GERAN.
- Therefore, the network **is not required** to include the Negotiated LLC SAPI IE.
- However, **if the UE indicates support for A/Gb mode**, then any network that supports S1-to-A/Gb mobility **shall include** the Negotiated LLC SAPI IE as part of the context transfer or handover preparation (e.g., in `Forward Relocation Request` or similar NAS transparent container).
- This ensures that upon entering A/Gb mode, the SM layer can correctly map active EPS bearers to PDP contexts using the pre-negotiated LLC SAPI.

#### 2. **Support of BSS Packet Flow Procedures**
- The second condition ("If the UE supports A/Gb mode **and** BSS packet flow procedures...") implies an **additional requirement** when advanced BSS features are supported.
- BSS packet flow procedures allow more granular control over packet scheduling and flow management in GERAN.
- When these are supported, the network may be required to signal additional parameters—including possibly more detailed LLC configuration—which reinforces the necessity of including the **Negotiated LLC SAPI IE**.
- Thus, **support for BSS packet flow procedures strengthens the obligation** to include the IE, but only if A/Gb mode itself is already supported.

---

### Expected Behavior:

- The **UE capability indication** (via UE Network Capability IE or similar) informs the MME about:
  - Whether it supports A/Gb mode
  - Whether it supports BSS packet flow procedures
- Based on this, the **MME determines** whether the target RNC/BSC needs LLC SAPI information.
- If the UE supports A/Gb mode, and the network supports S1-to-A/Gb mobility, then:
  - The MME **must include** the **Negotiated LLC SAPI IE** in relevant messages during handover preparation.
  - This allows the BSS to set up correct LLC links corresponding to each PDP context derived from EPS bearers.
- If the UE does **not** support A/Gb mode, the IE is **not included**, since inter-system change to A/Gb mode will not occur.

---

### Additional Consideration: Inter-System Change Procedure

From the context:
> "At inter-system change from S1 mode to A/Gb mode, SM shall not activate the PDP context(s) if SM does not have the following parameters from the active EPS bearer context(s):  
> – transaction identifier; and"

While LLC SAPI is not listed here as a mandatory activation condition, it is still **required for proper operation** in A/Gb mode. Its absence would impair data plane functionality even if activation proceeds.

Hence, the network must proactively include it **when UE capability permits or requires its use**.

---

### Conclusion:

> **The UE’s capability directly governs whether the network includes the Negotiated LLC SAPI IE during mobility from S1 to A/Gb mode.**

Specifically:
- ✅ **If the UE supports A/Gb mode**, then a network supporting S1-to-A/Gb mobility **shall include** the Negotiated LLC SAPI IE.
- ✅ **If the UE also supports BSS packet flow procedures**, this further mandates inclusion of such IEs related to LLC configuration.
- ❌ **If the UE does not support A/Gb mode**, the network is **not expected** to include the Negotiated LLC SAPI IE, as inter-system change to A/Gb mode is not possible.

Thus, **UE capability signaling acts as a trigger** for the network to include the Negotiated LLC SAPI IE — ensuring backward compatibility and efficient resource mapping during inter-RAT mobility.

results.question: What procedures can a UE in LIMITED-SERVICE state perform regarding cell selection and paging?
results.reference: The UE shall perform cell selection/reselection according to 3GPP TS 36.304 and may respond to paging using IMSI, though MUSIM UEs may optionally not respond based on paging message information like voice service indication.
results.model_answer:
A UE in the **LIMITED-SERVICE** substate shall perform the following procedures regarding **cell selection** and **paging**, based on 3GPP TS 24.301:

### ✅ Cell Selection:
- The UE **shall perform cell selection/reselection according to 3GPP TS 36.304 [21]**.
  - This includes monitoring and selecting suitable cells based on criteria defined in the physical layer and RRC specifications.
  - The goal is to find a cell that may allow for normal service or maintain limited service (e.g., emergency calls).

> *Rationale: This behavior is explicitly stated in multiple clauses describing EMM-DEREGISTERED substates, including LIMITED-SERVICE.*

---

### ✅ Paging:
- The UE **may respond to paging with IMSI**.
  - Specifically, it may respond to a **paging message received for the PS domain using IMSI or S-TMSI**.
  - However, this is **not mandatory**: the specification allows implementation-dependent behavior.

> *Note: As an implementation option, MUSIM UEs are allowed to not respond to paging based on information in the paging message (e.g., voice service indication).*

> *Source: Behavior inherited from general rules under EMM-DEREGISTERED.LIMITED-SERVICE state description.*

---

### 🔁 Additional Contextual Behavior:
While not directly related to cell selection or paging, the UE in **LIMITED-SERVICE** may also:
- Attempt to attach for **emergency bearer services** (including via local detach and re-attach).
- Attempt to attach for **access to RLOS (Roaming Limited Service)** — subject to specific handling rules in the context.

> *However, these actions do not override the core behaviors related to cell selection and paging.*

---

### ❌ What the UE Cannot Do:
- The UE **shall not send any user data**.
- The UE **shall not initiate most NAS signalling**, except:
  - A **service request** as a response to **paging**,
  - A **tracking area updating (TAU)** or **combined TAU** procedure,
  - Procedures triggered by upper layers for **emergency services** (e.g., emergency PDN connection, eCall, MMTEL emergency call, SMS over NAS/S102).

---

### Summary:

| Procedure                     | Allowed? | Details |
|------------------------------|----------|--------|
| **Cell selection/reselection** | ✅ Yes   | According to 3GPP TS 36.304 |
| **Respond to paging**         | ✅ Yes (optional) | May respond using IMSI or S-TMSI; implementation may choose not to respond |
| **Initiate arbitrary NAS procedures** | ❌ No | Only permitted exceptions apply |

Thus, in the **LIMITED-SERVICE** state, the UE remains capable of **performing cell selection/reselection** and **optionally responding to paging**, while being restricted from initiating most other NAS procedures unless justified by specific triggers like emergency calls or network-initiated paging.

results.question: How does the eCall inactivity procedure relate to a UE configured for eCall only mode in LIMITED-SERVICE state?
results.reference: If configured for eCall only mode as specified in 3GPP TS 31.102, the UE shall perform the eCall inactivity procedure when timer T3444 or T3445 expires.
results.model_answer:
The **eCall inactivity procedure** is **only applicable to a UE configured for eCall only mode** as defined in 3GPP TS 31.102 [17], and its execution is **triggered by the expiry of timers T3444 and/or T3445**, under specific EMM state and substate conditions.

To analyze how this procedure relates to a UE in the **LIMITED-SERVICE** substate, we must consider:

---

### 1. **When is the eCall inactivity procedure initiated?**

From the context:
> The eCall inactivity procedure shall be started when  
> - the UE is in any EMM-REGISTERED substate **except EMM-REGISTERED.PLMN-SEARCH or EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE**  
> - the UE is in EMM-IDLE mode; and  
> - one of the timer expiry conditions applies (T3444 and/or T3445 expired, with the other not running)

Thus, **the procedure can only start from an EMM-REGISTERED substate**, excluding PLMN-SEARCH and NO-CELL-AVAILABLE, and while in EMM-IDLE.

Now, **LIMITED-SERVICE** is one of the substates of **EMM-REGISTERED**, as per standard NAS behavior and implied in the text:
> "If the selected cell is known not to be able to provide normal service, the substate shall be LIMITED-SERVICE"

So, **LIMITED-SERVICE is an EMM-REGISTERED substate**, and unless excluded explicitly, it **is eligible** for triggering the eCall inactivity procedure — provided the other conditions are met.

---

### 2. **Is LIMITED-SERVICE excluded from triggering the procedure?**

The trigger condition excludes only two substates:
- EMM-REGISTERED.PLMN-SEARCH
- EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE

**LIMITED-SERVICE is not excluded.**

Therefore, **if the UE is in EMM-REGISTERED.LIMITED-SERVICE and in EMM-IDLE**, and either:
- T3444 expires and T3445 is not running,
- T3445 expires and T3444 is not running, or
- both have expired,

→ then the **eCall inactivity procedure shall be performed**.

---

### 3. **What happens during the eCall inactivity procedure?**

Upon triggering, the UE:
- Stops other timers (e.g., T3411, T3412)
- Performs a detach (EPS-only or combined, depending on registration)
- Deletes GUTI, TAI list, last visited TAI, equivalent PLMNs, eKSI
- Enters **EMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE**

This transition moves the UE out of the EMM-REGISTERED state entirely.

---

### 4. **Can a UE in LIMITED-SERVICE reach eCALL-INACTIVE?**

Yes — if:
- It is configured for **eCall only mode**
- It is in **EMM-IDLE.LIMITED-SERVICE**
- Timers **T3444 and/or T3445 expire** under the specified conditions

Then the procedure executes, leading to **EMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE**

Note: After entering eCALL-INACTIVE, the UE:
- Shall not initiate signaling except to originate an **eCall over IMS** or a **call to a non-emergency MSISDN/URI for test or reconfiguration**
- May still perform cell selection/reselection
- May respond to paging (implementation-dependent)

---

### 5. **Special Case: Power-On Behavior**

For a UE in eCall only mode:
> At power on, T3444 and T3445 are considered expired  
> After PLMN search, if a suitable cell is found but cannot provide normal service → enters **LIMITED-SERVICE**

But since timers are already expired, and if no action resets them, the **eCall inactivity procedure may be triggered immediately upon entering EMM-REGISTERED.LIMITED-SERVICE**, assuming the UE is in EMM-IDLE and no other timer prevents it.

However, typically, after successful attach (even in limited service), timers T3444/T3445 would be started. But for eCall-only UEs, these timers control inactivity, and their expiry leads to detachment and entry into eCALL-INACTIVE.

---

### ✅ Final Answer:

The **eCall inactivity procedure applies to a UE configured for eCall only mode even when in the LIMITED-SERVICE substate**, provided that:
- The UE is in **EMM-REGISTERED.LIMITED-SERVICE**
- The UE is in **EMM-IDLE mode**
- The triggering condition occurs: **T3444 and/or T3445 expires**, with the other not running

In such case, the UE **shall perform the eCall inactivity procedure**, which includes:
- Detaching (EPS-only or combined)
- Deleting mobility and security context
- Transitioning to **EMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE**

Thus, **LIMITED-SERVICE does not prevent** the execution of the eCall inactivity procedure — it is a valid starting point for it, as it is an EMM-REGISTERED substate not excluded by the specification.

results.question: What implementation option is specified for MUSIM UEs regarding paging response in LIMITED-SERVICE state?
results.reference: As an implementation option, a MUSIM UE is allowed to not respond to paging based on information available in the paging message, such as voice service indication.
results.model_answer:
In the **LIMITED-SERVICE** state, a MUSIM UE (Multi-USIM UE) is subject to specific constraints regarding its behavior toward paging, but the provided context does **not explicitly define** the UE’s paging response behavior *specifically for the LIMITED-SERVICE state*.

However, based on 3GPP TS 24.301 and the provided excerpts, we can analyze the relevant conditions:

- The **LIMITED-SERVICE** state typically occurs when a UE is camped on a suitable cell but not allowed full network services (e.g., due to lack of SIM authentication, or only emergency/RLOS access).
- From the context, one consistent **implementation option** across multiple states (including EMM-IDLE) is:
> **"As an implementation option, the MUSIM UE is allowed to not respond to paging based on the information available in the paging message, e.g. voice service indication."**

This note appears repeatedly in the context — associated with various procedures including:
- Service Request initiation
- Tracking Area Updating
- General paging response

Although the context does **not directly tie** this option to the **LIMITED-SERVICE** state, it is presented as a general **MUSIM-specific implementation flexibility**, applicable regardless of certain EMM substates, as long as the UE is MUSIM.

Moreover, in LIMITED-SERVICE:
- The UE may be attached only for **emergency bearer services** or **RLOS**.
- According to the specification, UEs attached for **RLOS** do **not support mobile terminated access** or **network-triggered service requests**.
- For **emergency bearer services**, the UE must remain capable of receiving paging for emergency call back (as per service continuity requirements), but even here, the **MUSIM implementation option** to **not respond to paging** based on content (e.g., non-voice, non-emergency) could still apply selectively.

### Conclusion:

The **only implementation option specified for MUSIM UEs regarding paging response** — which applies by extension unless explicitly restricted — is:

> **A MUSIM UE is allowed, as an implementation option, to not respond to paging based on the information available in the paging message, such as the voice service indication.**

This option is **not limited to a specific EMM state** in the text and is therefore considered valid across states, including LIMITED-SERVICE, unless contradicted by stronger constraints.

In **LIMITED-SERVICE**, while the UE may be restricted in what it can initiate, there is **no prohibition in the provided context** against applying this MUSIM-specific discretion in responding to paging.

---

### ✅ Final Answer:

**The specified implementation option for MUSIM UEs regarding paging response in the LIMITED-SERVICE state is: As an implementation option, the MUSIM UE is allowed to not respond to paging based on the information available in the paging message, e.g., voice service indication.**

results.question: How does a UE transition into the EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED state?
results.reference: The UE enters this state after it has initiated the service request procedure and is awaiting a response from the MME.
results.model_answer:
A User Equipment (UE) transitions into the **EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED** state when it successfully initiates the **Service Request procedure** by sending a NAS message to the MME, under specific conditions defined in 3GPP TS 24.301.

The transition occurs as follows:

### ✅ Conditions for Transition:
The UE enters the **EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED** state **after sending** one of the following messages and starting timer **T3417**, **T3417ext**, or **T3417ext-mt**, depending on the case:

---

### 1. **SERVICE REQUEST** or **EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST** with Service Type "Packet Services via S1"
This applies to **cases a, b, c, h, k, l, o** in clause 5.6.1.1:
- If the UE is **not configured for NAS signalling low priority**, it sends a **SERVICE REQUEST**.
- If the UE **is configured for NAS signalling low priority** and the network has indicated support for Extended Service Request (via last ATTACH ACCEPT or TAU ACCEPT), it sends an **EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST** with service type set to *"packet services via S1"*.
- After sending either message, the UE:
  - **Starts timer T3417**
  - **Enters EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED**

> 📌 Note: A UE configured for dual priority is considered configured for NAS signalling low priority.

---

### 2. **EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST** for CS Fallback (Mobile Originating)
This applies to **case d** in clause 5.6.1.1:
- The UE sends an **EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST** due to mobile originating CS fallback.
- It then:
  - **Starts timer T3417ext**
  - **Enters EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED**

---

### 3. **EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST** for Paging Response (CS Fallback)
This applies to **case e** in clause 5.6.1.1:
- If the UE is in **EMM-IDLE mode**, it sends an **EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST** in response to paging for CS fallback.
  - **Starts T3417ext-mt**
  - **Enters EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED**
- If the UE is in **EMM-CONNECTED mode** and accepts the paging:
  - Sends **EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST** with CSFB response = *"accepted"*
  - **Starts T3417ext-mt**
  - **Enters EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED**
- If it rejects the paging, it does **not** enter this state — instead, it remains in **EMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE**.

---

### 4. **EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST** for Other Cases
For **cases f, g, i, j** in clause 5.6.1.1:
- The UE sends an **EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST** (e.g., for PS handover, IMS voice EPS fallback, etc.)
- Then:
  - **Starts T3417**
  - **Enters EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED**

---

### 5. **EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST** for NAS Signalling Connection Release or Rejection of Paging
For **cases p and q** in clause 5.6.1.1:
- The UE sends an **EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST** to release NAS signalling connection or reject paging.
- Then:
  - **Starts T3417**
  - **Enters EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED**

---

### ⚠️ Important Notes:
- The **EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED** state is **only entered after successful transmission** of the appropriate request message.
- The UE must **not be running another EMM-specific procedure** (e.g., Attach or Tracking Area Update) — only one UE-initiated EMM-specific procedure can run at a time.
- The state is **transient**: it ends upon receiving **SERVICE ACCEPT**, **SERVICE REJECT**, timeout of T3417/T3417ext/T3417ext-mt, or other abnormal cases (e.g., lower layer failure, detach collision).

---

### Summary Table:

| Trigger | Message Sent | Timer Started | Enters EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED? |
|--------|--------------|----------------|----------------------------------------|
| MO data/signalling (non-low-priority) | SERVICE REQUEST | T3417 | ✅ |
| MO data/signalling (low-priority, supported) | EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST | T3417 | ✅ |
| MO CS fallback | EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST | T3417ext | ✅ |
| Paging response for CSFB (idle/connected, accepted) | EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST | T3417ext-mt | ✅ |
| Various EMM-CM procedures (f, g, i, j) | EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST | T3417 | ✅ |
| NAS conn release or paging rejection (p, q) | EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST | T3417 | ✅ |

---

### Conclusion:
> The UE transitions into the **EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED** state **immediately after transmitting** a **SERVICE REQUEST**, **CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST**, or **EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST** message for any applicable use case defined in clause 5.6.1.1, provided no other EMM-specific procedure is ongoing, and subsequently starts the appropriate T3417-family timer.

results.question: Why would a UE be in the EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED state?
results.reference: Because it has started the service request procedure and is currently waiting for the MME to respond.
results.model_answer:
A User Equipment (UE) enters the **EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED** state when it begins the **service request procedure** to transition from **EMM-IDLE** mode to **EMM-CONNECTED** mode, or while in **EMM-CONNECTED** mode to reactivate a NAS signaling connection for specific purposes.

This state indicates that the UE has initiated the procedure and is awaiting a response from the MME (Mobility Management Entity). The primary reasons for entering this state are:

### 1. **To Establish or Reactivate a NAS Signaling Connection**
The service request procedure is used to:
- Resume a suspended EMM context.
- Re-establish radio and S1 bearers after the UE was in EMM-IDLE.
- Respond to an incoming **paging** message (mobile terminated call or data).
- Initiate **mobile originated services**, such as:
  - Requesting user plane resources (e.g., for data transmission).
  - Sending an SMS over NAS.
  - Initiating a CS fallback (CSFB) or 1xCS fallback.
  - Activating a PDN connection.

Once the UE sends the **SERVICE REQUEST**, **EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST**, or **CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST** message, it starts timer **T3417**, **T3417ext**, or **T3417ext-mt**, and transitions into the **EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED** state.

---

### 2. **Triggering Conditions Based on Use Case**
According to TS 24.301 clause 5.6.1, the UE initiates the service request procedure (and thus enters this state) in various cases, including:

- **Case a**: Response to a paging request from the network (MT access).
- **Case b**: Need to transmit uplink data (MO user plane service).
- **Case c**: Upper layer request for signaling (e.g., SMS over NAS).
- **Case d**: Retransmission of a previous failed service request (using T3417ext).
- **Case e**: Response to paging while already in EMM-CONNECTED (e.g., CSFB acceptance/rejection).
- **Cases f, i, j**: Abnormal case recovery (e.g., tracking area update required during ongoing service request).
- **Cases p, q**: NAS signaling connection release or rejection of paging with preference indication.

For most of these cases, after sending the appropriate request message, the specification explicitly states:  
> *"the UE shall start [a T3417-type] timer and enter the state EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED."*

---

### 3. **Protocol Behavior in This State**
While in **EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED**, the UE:
- Waits for a response from the network (e.g., SERVICE ACCEPT, SERVICE REJECT, or implicit success via downlink NAS transport).
- May retransmit the request upon timeout of T3417 (up to 5 attempts unless otherwise constrained).
- Handles abnormal events like:
  - TAI change → triggers tracking area update.
  - Detach request received → may abort or handle based on detach type.
  - Lower layer failure → aborts procedure and acts accordingly (e.g., attempts RAT selection for CSFB).

The state persists until:
- A **SERVICE ACCEPT** is received → UE moves to **EMM-REGISTERED**.
- A **SERVICE REJECT** is received or timer expires → UE aborts and returns to **EMM-REGISTERED** or another appropriate state.
- Another higher-priority procedure (e.g., tracking area update) interrupts it.

---

### Summary
The UE is in **EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED** because:
> It has sent a service request message (SERVICE REQUEST, EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST, or CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST) to the MME to establish or resume connectivity, and is now waiting for a response, with associated timer(s) running.

This state is central to mobility and session management in LTE NAS, enabling efficient transition between idle and connected modes while handling diverse service initiation scenarios.

results.question: What procedural context defines the EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED state for a UE?
results.reference: The state is defined by the UE having commenced the service request procedure and being in a waiting period for an MME response.
results.model_answer:
The **EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED** state is defined within the procedural context of the **Service Request procedure** in E-UTRAN (S1 mode), as specified in 3GPP TS 24.301.

### Procedural Context:
This state is entered by the UE **immediately after it sends a SERVICE REQUEST, CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST, or EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST message**, and before receiving a successful response (e.g., SERVICE ACCEPT) or a rejection (SERVICE REJECT) from the network.

It represents an **intermediate transient state** during which the UE is awaiting a response from the MME to complete the service request procedure.

---

### Entry Conditions:
The UE enters the **EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED** state upon transmission of one of the following messages, depending on the triggering case (as per clause 5.6.1.1):

- **SERVICE REQUEST**  
  - For cases a, b, c, h, k, l, o when NAS signalling low priority is not configured or not supported.
- **EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST**  
  - For all other cases in clause 5.6.1.1 (including d, e, f, g, i, j, p, q, and o with specific conditions).
- **CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST**  
  - In NB-S1 mode, for control plane CIoT EPS optimization.

Upon sending any of these messages, the UE:
1. Starts the appropriate timer:
   - **T3417** – for most service requests.
   - **T3417ext** – for CS fallback initiated by paging (case d).
   - **T3417ext-mt** – for mobile terminating CS fallback (case e).
2. Transitions to **EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED**.

---

### Purpose of the State:
This state ensures that:
- Only one service request can be active at a time.
- The UE does not initiate conflicting EMM procedures (e.g., tracking area update unless triggered by TAI change).
- Proper handling of collisions (e.g., with detach or paging responses).
- Correct processing of retransmissions, timeouts, or rejections.

---

### Exit Conditions:
The UE exits this state based on:
1. **Successful completion**: Receipt of **SERVICE ACCEPT**, leading to **EMM-REGISTERED**.
2. **Rejection**: Receipt of **SERVICE REJECT**, leading to various states depending on cause (e.g., EMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE, EMM-DEREGISTERED, etc.).
3. **Timer expiry**:
   - T3417 → triggers retransmission attempts (up to 4).
   - T3417ext / T3417ext-mt expiry leads to fallback actions (e.g., GERAN/UTRAN selection for CSFB).
4. **Abnormal cases**:
   - Lower layer failure.
   - Detach collision.
   - TAI change requiring tracking area update.
   - "Extended wait time" received.

---

### Key Constraints from Specification:
- The service request procedure (and thus this state) **cannot be initiated if another UE-initiated EMM specific procedure** (e.g., attach, tracking area update) is ongoing.
- While in this state, **transport of NAS messages is blocked** unless piggybacked appropriately.
- The network may reject the service request only **before initiating procedures interpreted by the UE as successful completion** (e.g., bearer setup).

---

### Summary:
> The **EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED** state is part of the **Service Request procedure (S1 mode)** and is entered when the UE transmits a **SERVICE REQUEST, EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST, or CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST** message. It reflects the transient phase where the UE awaits network response, manages retransmissions, handles collisions, and enforces access restrictions — central to mobility and session management in EMM-IDLE to EMM-CONNECTED transition.

results.question: What are the two key conditions that characterize the UE's EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED state?
results.reference: The UE has started the service request procedure, and it is waiting for a response from the MME.
results.model_answer:
The UE's **EMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED** state is characterized by the following two key conditions:

1.  **A Service Request message has been sent:** The UE has transmitted either a `SERVICE REQUEST`, `EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST`, or `CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST` message to the MME, initiating the procedure to transition from EMM-IDLE to EMM-CONNECTED mode (or to handle CS/1xCS fallback).

2.  **Waiting for a response from the network:** The UE is actively waiting for a response from the network (such as a `SERVICE ACCEPT`, `SERVICE REJECT`, `SECURITY MODE COMMAND`, or an indication from the lower layers) before the service request procedure can be considered complete.

This state represents the transitional phase between sending the initial request and receiving confirmation of its success, failure, or rejection. The state ends when the procedure completes successfully (transitioning to EMM-CONNECTED), is rejected by the network (triggering actions based on the cause value), or times out/fails due to lower layer issues.

results.question: How does the network initiate the dedicated EPS bearer context activation procedure?
results.reference: The network initiates the procedure by sending an ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message to the UE.
results.model_answer:
The network initiates the dedicated EPS bearer context activation procedure by sending an **ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST** message to the UE.

Specifically:

- The **MME** (Mobility Management Entity) initiates the procedure.
- The MME sends the **ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST** message over the NAS (Non-Access Stratum) interface.
- Upon sending this message, the MME:
  - Allocates an **EPS bearer identity** (as per clause 9.3.2 of the specification),
  - Includes the **linked EPS bearer identity**, which refers to the EPS bearer identity of the associated default EPS bearer context,
  - Starts the timer **T3485**,
  - Enters the state **BEARER CONTEXT ACTIVE PENDING**.

If the procedure was triggered in response to a UE-initiated request (e.g., via the *UE requested bearer resource allocation* or *bearer resource modification* procedure), the MME includes the same **Procedure Transaction Identity (PTI)** that was received from the UE in the original request.

This procedure can occur:
- During the attach procedure (in parallel with default bearer activation),
- After successful attachment,
- Together with the service request procedure,
- But not in NB-S1 mode (narrowband S1 mode), where dedicated bearer context activation is not used.

Thus, the initiation is unambiguously performed by the network (MME) via transmission of the **ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST** message containing appropriate parameters, followed by timer start and state transition.

results.question: Why does the UE send an ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT message during this procedure?
results.reference: The UE sends this message to confirm the successful activation of the dedicated EPS bearer context requested by the network.
results.model_answer:
The UE sends an **ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT** message to acknowledge the successful activation of a dedicated EPS bearer context as instructed by the network via the **ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST** message.

According to 3GPP TS 24.301, upon receipt and successful processing of the **ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST**, the UE is required to:

- Validate the received parameters (e.g., check that the linked EPS bearer identity corresponds to an active default bearer).
- Process the received Traffic Flow Template (TFT) and apply uplink traffic flow mapping to the new radio bearer.
- Handle any optional protocol configuration options (e.g., APN rate control parameters, QoS rules for inter-system change).
- Stop timer T3396 under specific conditions related to APN usage and request type (unless it's an emergency PDN connection).
- Release any associated traffic flow aggregate description if the PTI in the request matches a previously initiated UE-requested procedure.

After completing these actions and verifying that the requested bearer can be activated, the UE **must send the ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT** message to inform the network that the dedicated bearer has been successfully established at the UE side.

This message serves as a **positive acknowledgment** in the ESM (EPS Session Management) signaling procedure. It allows the MME to transition from a waiting state (typically with timer T3485 running) to the **BEARER CONTEXT ACTIVE** state. Upon receiving this ACCEPT message, the MME stops timer T3485 and considers the dedicated bearer activation complete.

Thus, the purpose of sending the **ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT** is:
- To confirm correct reception and processing of the activation command.
- To synchronize the EPS bearer context state between UE and network.
- To allow the network to proceed with后续 procedures (e.g., QoS enforcement in the core network, potential follow-up modifications).

In summary:  
👉 **The UE sends the ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT message to complete the successful execution of the dedicated bearer activation procedure, as mandated by the ESM protocol in TS 24.301.**

results.question: How does the network conclude the dedicated EPS bearer context activation procedure?
results.reference: The network concludes the procedure upon receiving the ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT message from the UE.
results.model_answer:
The network concludes the **dedicated EPS bearer context activation procedure** upon successful receipt of the **ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT** message from the UE.

### Detailed Procedure Flow (from the network/MME perspective):

1. The MME initiates the procedure by sending an **ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST** message to the UE.
2. The MME starts **timer T3485** and enters the state **BEARER CONTEXT ACTIVE PENDING**.
3. The UE processes the request:
   - If accepted, the UE responds with an **ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT**.
   - If rejected, the UE sends an **ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT**, including an appropriate ESM cause.
4. Upon receiving the **ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT**:
   - The MME **stops timer T3485**.
   - The MME transitions the EPS bearer context to the state **BEARER CONTEXT ACTIVE**.
   - The dedicated EPS bearer context activation procedure is considered **successfully completed**.

---

### Abnormal Cases That May Prevent Conclusion:

- **T3485 expiry**:  
  On first expiry, the MME retransmits the REQUEST. This is repeated up to four times. On the **fifth expiry**, the MME **aborts** the procedure, releases resources, and sets the bearer context to **INACTIVE**.

- **Reception of ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT**:  
  The MME stops T3485, aborts the procedure, releases radio resources, and enters **BEARER CONTEXT INACTIVE**.

- **Collision with PDN disconnect request**:  
  If the MME receives a PDN DISCONNECT REQUEST for the same PDN during the activation, it terminates the activation procedure and proceeds with disconnect.

---

### Summary:

✅ **Normal conclusion**:  
→ Receipt of **ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT** from UE  
→ Stop T3485  
→ Enter **BEARER CONTEXT ACTIVE** state  
→ Procedure complete

❌ **Abnormal termination**:  
→ T3485 expires 5 times  
→ REJECT message received  
→ Collision with PDN disconnect  

Thus, the **network concludes the procedure successfully only when it receives the ACCEPT message within the T3485 timeout period**.

results.question: Under what conditions can a UE send an UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT message while timer T3346 is running?
results.reference: The UE can send the message only if it is configured to use AC11-15 in the selected PLMN, has an emergency PDN connection established, or is configured for dual priority with a non-low-priority PDN connection and T3346 was started due to a low-priority NAS request.
results.model_answer:
A UE **shall not** send an **UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT** message while **timer T3346 is running**, **unless** one of the following conditions is met:

1. **The UE is configured to use access class 11–15 (AC11–15)** in the selected PLMN.  
   *(This allows high-priority access during congestion, bypassing the restriction imposed by T3346.)*

2. **The UE has a PDN connection for emergency bearer services established.**  
   *(Emergency services are exempt from congestion control restrictions.)*

3. **The UE is configured for dual priority and:**
   - It has a PDN connection established **without low access priority**, **and**
   - Timer T3346 was started in response to a NAS signalling request that had the **"low priority" indicator set** (i.e., the congestion back-off applies only to low-priority requests).

> In all other cases, the UE **must defer** sending the UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT message until:
> - Timer T3346 **expires**, or
> - Timer T3346 is **stopped** (e.g., due to entering a new PLMN that is not equivalent, or due to network-initiated procedures overriding the back-off).

---

### Supporting Rationale from 3GPP TS 24.301:
- Timer **T3346** is the **mobility management back-off timer**, used by the network to control NAS signalling overload.
- When active, it restricts the UE from initiating most mobility and transport procedures, including **UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT**, except for specific **exempted cases** related to **emergency services**, **high-priority access (AC11–15)**, or **dual-priority logic** where the current request is not subject to low priority.
- The context explicitly states:  
  > "The UE shall not send an UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT message unless [...] [one of the three conditions above]"
- Furthermore:  
  > "The UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT message can be sent, if still necessary, when timer T3346 expires or is stopped."

Thus, these exceptions are **strictly limited** to the three defined conditions. No other triggers permit transmission during T3346 operation.

results.question: How does timer T3447 affect the transmission of UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT messages when the UE is in EMM-CONNECTED mode?
results.reference: When T3447 is running and the UE is in EMM-CONNECTED mode, the UE is prohibited from sending the message unless it is configured for AC11-15, has an emergency PDN connection, or has received a network-initiated signalling message.
results.model_answer:
Timer T3447 (Service Gap Control timer) imposes restrictions on the transmission of **UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT** messages when the UE is in **EMM-CONNECTED mode**, specifically after the UE has transitioned from EMM-IDLE to EMM-CONNECTED following a prior release of the NAS signalling connection under active Service Gap Control (SGC).

### Key Effect of Timer T3447:
When **T3447 is running**, the UE **shall not send an UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT message** while in **EMM-CONNECTED mode**, **unless one of the following exceptions applies**:

1. ✅ The UE is **configured to use AC11/AC15 (high priority access)** in the selected PLMN;  
2. ✅ A **network-initiated signalling message** (e.g., DOWNLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT) has been received; or  
3. ✅ (Context-specific) If the UE attached **without a PDN connection**, this restriction applies more strictly — but even then, the above two conditions still allow transmission.

> ⚠️ Note: Unlike T3346, there is **no exception for emergency PDN connections** in the T3447 clause related to *generic* NAS transport (though such an exception exists for other procedures/messages).

### When Can Transmission Resume?
The **UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT** message **can be sent, if still necessary, when timer T3447 expires**. The UE must defer the transmission until then unless one of the above exceptions is met.

Additionally:
- The **timer continues to run** even if the UE transitions between EMM-IDLE and EMM-CONNECTED modes.
- If the UE receives a **network-initiated message** (e.g., paging followed by downlink NAS transport), this breaks the restriction, allowing the UE to respond with uplink generic NAS transport if needed.

---

### Summary of Behavior:
| Condition | Can UE Send UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT? |
|--------|--------------------------------------------|
| T3447 running + UE in EMM-CONNECTED mode | ❌ No (restricted) |
| T3447 running + UE in EMM-CONNECTED mode + UE uses AC11/AC15 | ✅ Yes |
| T3447 running + UE in EMM-CONNECTED mode + network-initiated message received | ✅ Yes |
| T3447 expired/stopped | ✅ Yes (restriction lifted) |

Thus, **T3447 acts as a rate-limiting mechanism** to control how frequently UEs can initiate certain NAS signalling (including generic transport) after being in connected mode, primarily to mitigate signaling overload due to frequent wake-ups or reporting from IoT-type devices.

This behavior aligns with the broader purpose of **Service Gap Control (SGC)** defined in TS 23.401 and enforced via T3447 in TS 24.301.

results.question: What must occur for a UE to send an UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT message after timer T3346 was started, if the message was initially restricted?
results.reference: The UE must wait until timer T3346 expires or is stopped before it can send the message, provided the transmission is still necessary at that time.
results.model_answer:
For a UE to send an **UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT** message *after* timer **T3346 was started**, when the message was initially restricted (i.e., the UE was prohibited from sending it due to T3346 being active), the following **must occur** — per 3GPP TS 24.301 (specifically clause 5.6.1.5 and related abnormal case handling):

### ✅ Required Condition:
> **Timer T3346 must expire or be explicitly stopped.**

This is stated unambiguously in the specification text:

> *"The UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT message can be sent, if still necessary, when timer T3346 expires or is stopped."*  
> *(First context block, subclause a)*  
>  
> *"The UPLINK NAS TRANSPORT message can be sent, if still necessary, when timer T3346 expires or is stopped."*  
> *(Second context block, subclause a — note: "UPLINK NAS TRANSPORT" here is used generically in some contexts but aligns with "UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT" for generic transport; the restriction logic and recovery condition are identical and co-located in the spec.)*

### 🔍 Why this is the *only* mandatory condition (and why alternatives do *not* suffice):
- **No exception permits transmission *while* T3346 is running**, except for the three narrow exemptions listed *before* the “unless” clause — but those are **preconditions for *allowing* transmission *despite* T3346 running**, not post-hoc enablers:
  - UE configured to use AC11–15 in selected PLMN  
  - UE has PDN connection for emergency bearer services established  
  - UE is dual-priority configured *and* has non-low-priority PDN connection, *and* T3346 was started in response to a NAS signalling request *with low access priority*  

  → These are **static state-based exceptions** that *bypass* the restriction *if true at the time of attempt*. They do *not* describe what must happen *after* T3346 starts — they are alternative eligibility paths, not recovery actions.

- **T3346 expiry/stop is the universal recovery mechanism** for cases where *none* of those exceptions apply. The spec consistently uses the phrase *"can be sent, if still necessary, when timer T3346 expires or is stopped"* — indicating this is the *only* normative recovery trigger for the restricted state.

- **No other timer (e.g., T3447) or event (e.g., paging, RRC release, network-initiated signalling) lifts the T3346 restriction on UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT.**  
  - T3447 governs *different* restrictions (e.g., on UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT *in EMM-CONNECTED mode after attach without PDN*, or *after NAS signalling connection release*), but its expiry does *not* override T3346’s prohibition. The two timers operate orthogonally; T3346 takes precedence for its defined scope (low-priority NAS signalling congestion control).
  - Receiving a DOWNLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT *does* stop T3440 (per context), but no clause states it stops or overrides T3346.

- **“Stopped” means explicit deactivation** — e.g., via:
  - Receipt of a network command (though spec doesn’t define such a command for T3346),
  - Transition into a state where the timer is no longer applicable (e.g., successful attach/TAU with resolution of low-priority condition), or
  - Implementation-specific internal cancellation (but only if aligned with spec-mandated conditions — e.g., upon establishment of emergency PDN, which satisfies an exemption, *not* as a general stop).

However, **the spec does *not* define any network-triggered mechanism to *stop* T3346 early** — unlike T3440 or T3447, which are explicitly stopped by downlink NAS messages (e.g., DOWNLINK NAS TRANSPORT). T3346 is purely UE-local and runs to expiry unless one of the exemption conditions holds *at send time*.

---

### ✅ Therefore, the precise answer is:

**The UE may send the UPLINK GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT message only after timer T3346 has either expired or been stopped — and only if the message is still necessary (i.e., the upper-layer application request remains pending).**  
No other event or condition (e.g., receiving paging, entering EMM-CONNECTED, or expiry of another timer) authorizes transmission while T3346 is running *unless* one of the three specified exemptions applies *concurrently*. But the question asks what must occur *after* T3346 was started *when the message was initially restricted* — implying the exemptions *do not hold*. Hence, **expiry or stop of T3346 is the sole required condition**.

This reflects the core design intent of T3346: to enforce a mandatory backoff period following low-priority NAS signalling rejection (e.g., due to congestion), preventing repeated attempts until the network-specified wait time elapses.

results.question: Under what condition would a UE include the DRX parameter in NB-S1 mode IE during a tracking area updating procedure?
results.reference: The UE would include this IE during a tracking area updating procedure only if it is not a periodic tracking area updating procedure. The clause explicitly excludes inclusion when performing a periodic tracking area updating procedure.
results.model_answer:
